verses.text: Vindicate me, O LORD! For I have walked with integrity; I have trusted in the LORD without wavering.
Test me, O LORD, and try me; examine my heart and mind.
For Your loving devotion is before my eyes, and I have walked in Your truth.
I do not sit with deceitful men, nor keep company with hypocrites.
I hate the mob of evildoers, and refuse to sit with the wicked.
I wash my hands in innocence that I may go about Your altar, O LORD,
to raise my voice in thanksgiving and declare all Your wonderful works.
O LORD, I love the house where You dwell, the place where Your glory resides.
Do not take my soul away with sinners, or my life with men of bloodshed,
in whose hands are wicked schemes, whose right hands are full of bribes.
But I will walk with integrity; redeem me and be merciful to me.
My feet stand on level ground; in the congregations I will bless the LORD.

context.author: The title says “of David” (Hebrew le-David), which can mean by David, for David or about David. Seventy-three psalms carry his name; tradition and the New Testament take many of them as his.
context.genre: Psalm: a song or prayer in Hebrew poetry
context.audience: Israel at worship in Jerusalem, and every reader who prays
context.setting: “Vindicate me, O LORD! For I have walked with integrity” (v.1). David invites God’s inspection: “Test me, O LORD, and try me; examine my heart and mind” (v.2). He has kept away from deceitful men and the mob of evildoers (vv.4-5). “I wash my hands in innocence that I may go about Your altar, O LORD” (v.6), singing thanks. “O LORD, I love the house where You dwell, the place where Your glory resides” (v.8). He asks not to be swept away with the bloodthirsty, whose hands are full of bribes (vv.9-10), and ends standing firm: “My feet stand on level ground; in the congregations I will bless the LORD” (v.12).
context.custom: Washing the hands was a public sign of innocence: elders washed their hands over a heifer to declare that they had not shed innocent blood (Deuteronomy 21:6-7). Priests washed before approaching the altar (Exodus 30:19-21). Processions walked around the altar in worship.
context.timelineImmediate: Psalm 27 declares, “The LORD is my light and my salvation—whom shall I fear?”
context.timelineBible: Pilate washed his hands before the crowd and said, “I am innocent of this man’s blood” (Matthew 27:24), using the old gesture while handing Jesus over. Psalm 139 ends with the same request as v.2: “Search me, O God, and know my heart” (Psalm 139:23).

translation.meaning: To examine, test, try as metal is tested.

gospelParallels.note: Pilate washes his hands before the crowd.
Lift up holy hands without anger.

otBackground.note: Elders wash their hands to declare innocence.
Priests wash before going to the altar.
Search me, O God, and know my heart.

overview.summary: David asks God to test him and vindicate him, washes his hands in innocence, and declares his love for God’s house.
overview.settingLine: At the altar with washed hands.

history.t: A charge brought against an innocent man.

archaeology.t: Horned stone altars have been found at Beersheba, Dan and Megiddo.
Large bronze and stone basins stood in temple courts.

overview.discussion: David asks God to examine his heart (v.2). Would I invite that kind of inspection? What might God find?
overview.book: The book of Psalms · 150 psalms (1-80 in the app so far). Israel’s songs and prayers: praise, lament, thanks, trust and wisdom, many of them by David.
overview.author: David
